newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Foster's plans buyback,BHP sells stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Foster's plans buyback,BHP sells stake.

text.p: Foster's Brewing Group Ltd said on Thursday that it would buy back 254.5 million of its shares from Asahi Breweries for A$625 million.

The leading Australian brewer said it would pay A$2.49 per share for the Asahi stake, which represents the bulk of its 270.3 million shareholding, equivalent to about 13 percent of the fully paid shares. Certain agreed costs would be deducted.

Foster's also said 36.5 percent shareholder Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd would place 86 percent of its 716.6 million Foster's shareholding to institutions at A$2.49 per share. It would offer the other 100 million shares to BHP shareholders.

Foster's asked the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) earlier on Thursday afternoon for a trading halt to be placed on its shares pending an announcement which would affect more than 50 percent of its issued capital.
The company said the buyback deal with Asahi was part of an arrangement in which the Japanese brewer and BHP had committed to dispose of all their Foster's shares.

Foster's president and chief executive officer Ted Kunkel said the Asahi buyback price represented a five percent discount to Foster's average price in calendar 1997. Foster's shares were three cents at A$2.60 ahead of the trading halt.

Foster's said the repurchase of the Asahi shares would require the approval of eligible shareholders and a buyback resolution would be put to a general meeting on July 24. BHP and Asahi cannot vote at the meeting.
The company also said an independent experts report from Grant Samuel and Associates had advised that the buyback proposal was fair and reasonable to non-associated shareholders.
Foster's has a market capitalisation of A$5.10 billion based on 1.96 billion shares outstanding.
